title: Online Learning for Dynamic Structural Characterization in Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy
problem: High-speed in-situ EELS data acquisition (400 fps) with low SNR requires real-time processing for dynamic structural tracking without offline training bottleneck.
motivation: Materials science needs fast, on-device characterization of nanoscale structural changes in high-throughput EELS data.
method: Spiking neural network (SNN)-based Variational Autoencoder (VAE) embeds spectral data for structural prediction with online learning implemented on FPGA, achieving 28.3 dB SNR and 25.2×–93.7× latency reduction.
key_novelty: First fully online learning hardware solution combining SNNs with VAEs for real-time EELS structural tracking without offline training.
contributions: SNN-VAE framework for EELS spectral denoising and structural prediction
28.3 dB SNR achievement in MXene annealing data
FPGA hardware implementation with full online learning capability
25.2× latency reduction, 93.7× on full hardware, 4.5× energy savings vs baseline
limitations: Validation limited to MXene annealing dataset; generalization to other materials characterization unclear.
primary_theme: online SNN-VAE on FPGA for materials characterization
